Assembly implications

The isolated hinge stage defers wall attachment. Its nominal geometry supports forming/holding access before the hardware is joined to a wall, within these nose envelopes. An actual alignment/heading fixture and subsequent joining process remain unresolved.

The wall-module and completed-cage stages expose why late heading cannot simply be assumed. The common pivot axis is 4 mm inward of the modeled wall face; a constant-radius body larger than 8 mm reaches that wall when its approach runs alongside it. Neighboring walls block the tested straight approaches on completed cages. A reduced/tapered nose or another approach could behave differently; this study does not search every tool shape or route.

Installed-context results include the full nominal pan shell, pickup and tube proxies with the cover removed. No OEM mount/boss or fastener tool access is inferred.

Scope and sources

Exact continuous cylindrical nose-sweep intersection from each saved pin outer face outward to beyond every obstacle AABB.

Body-sized cylindrical assumptions, not complete tools. Cup geometry, jaws, hands/gun, weld beads, forming force, material rating and tolerances are unmodeled. OEM mount/fastener access is not tested.

Approaches extend at least 150 mm and finish at least 10 mm beyond every obstacle's projected bounding box. The geometric cylinder is a continuous sweep; other gate/path checks retain their separate sampling limits.

See tool-source and dimensional assumptions. The 9.525/12.7 mm values are conversions of cataloged tool-body diameters. Cup/nose shape and stainless-pin applicability are unknown. See *_pin_access.step under concepts/p4/STEP/ for representative overlays.
